history: First full run at 10 / 40 / 120 req/s: the stack answered at 10 req/s (p50 0.8 s) and collapsed at 40 (16 % failed, 2,425 iterations dropped) with the API's loop delay p99 near 43 ms throughout. Rates lowered to 5 / 20 / 60.

Three diagnostic runs showed the same workload giving caller p50 of 39 ms, 226 ms and 235 ms on different occasions; Postgres sessions were mostly idle in transaction, waiting on the API. A host-to-container round-trip calibration, a /health control and a pg_stat_activity sampler were added.

Final run at 5 / 20 / 60 req/s: normal p95 0.5 s, peak p95 6.3 s (1 % failed), spike p50 12.7 s (12 % failed), soak 10 minutes 0 failures with flat memory; loop delay p99 25 to 33 ms in every profile.

results.suite: tools/event-loop-audit/scrape-demo.mjs --stall (real Prometheus v2.55.0 + Alertmanager v0.27.0, the built API, worker and probe as separate processes, Postgres and Redis containers, a local HTTP receiver)
results.status: PASSED after one fix to the demo itself
history: Earlier branch (API and worker only, no Alertmanager, no probe): run 1 21/21, run 2 23/24 (EventLoopBlockingWithImpact did not fire because the request histogram cannot see queueing; rule fixed), run 3 25/25.

This branch, full run with --stall (about 35 minutes): 40/41. The one FAIL, 'a healthy /health reads fast from the probe', read the quantile before rate() had two samples (n/a): a timing bug in the demo, not in the probe. Every other check passed, including WorkerEventLoopBlockingWithQueueImpact from a real worker stall with 20,000 queued jobs, EventLoopLongStallCritical from a real 12 s block, ApiCallerLatencyHigh, and firing plus resolved notifications at the receiver.

Fix: the demo waits for the quantile (up to 60 s). Rerun without the stall phases (about 10 minutes): 26/26, the probe's healthy /health p95 reads 0.024 s. The stall phases were NOT rerun after that fix; evidence/scrape-demo.json is the 40/41 full run.
